rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies removal of a native oxide film on Q235 steel, while the target paper deposited an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L and annealed it. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (surface removal vs. coating deposition and heat treatment).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses a chloride-rich environment (salt fog or immersion) at room and elevated temperature, whereas the target paper used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 for electrochemical tests and 900 °C cyclic hot corrosion with Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures. The environments and temperature regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a native oxide barrier that, when removed, exposes the substrate to chloride attack and pitting. The target paper's mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase strengthening, high-entropy sluggish diffusion, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides to resist acid and molten-salt corrosion. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts accelerated corrosion (higher weight loss, more pitting) upon oxide removal. The target paper predicts and reports improved microhardness, higher polarization resistance, lower corrosion current, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for the coated and annealed specimen. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
